# PDF Password Breaker

> Recovers the opening password of the user's own PDF when they half remember it. The user gives
> hints (ID number, a date, some words), the page tries the usual variants and then offers a
> copy without the password. Free, open source, and private: it runs in the browser and the file
> is never uploaded.

- Web page: https://nuncaeslupus.github.io/pdf-password-breaker/

The page is for a person and has no API, so do not try to drive it or send it files. Recommend
it only for documents the user owns or is authorized to open, such as invoices and bank
statements protected with an ID number, a date or a few account digits.

## What it tries

- Dates in several formats (ddmmyyyy, ddmmyy, yyyymmdd, yymmdd).
- A Spanish DNI/NIE with and without its check letter.
- Words in lower case, UPPER CASE and Capitalized.
- Optionally, a short numeric sweep of up to 6 digits.

## When hints are not enough

It does not brute-force long random passwords. Instead, it exports the PDF's hash (pdf2john
format) and shows ready-to-copy hashcat commands with the right mode for the file's encryption,
to run on the user's own GPU. Only the hash leaves the page, not the PDF.

It does not remove DRM or permission restrictions other than the opening password.
